question: Where should a keyed value's curve open: inside its lane on the timeline, or in a Graph panel on the right as the video mock draws it?
context: Built in the lane because the task asked for a curve view on a lane. The video mock puts it in a Graph group on the right.

options.label: In the lane
options.summary: Click the curve button on a lane, or Graph in Animating, and that lane grows taller and shows the curve right on the timeline, lined up with the clip and the playhead. This is what is built now.
pros: The curve lines up with the ruler, the clip and the playhead
Nothing extra to open on the right
The way After Effects shows curves in its timeline
cons: The timeline gets taller and may need scrolling
options.mitigation: The lane opens only when asked, and closes with the same button.

options.label: Graph panel on the right
options.summary: The curve lives in a collapsed Graph group at the bottom of the Properties panel, as video.html draws it. It shows the picked value across the clip, and clicking a value name in Animating chooses which one it plots.
cons: The curve cannot line up with the timeline, so times have to be read off its own labels
The panel is narrow, about 210 points, so the curve is small
options.mitigation: Label the start, middle and end times under the curve, as the mock does.

options.label: Both
options.summary: Keep the curve in the lane and also add the mock's Graph panel on the right, each showing the same curve.
pros: Everyone finds it where they look
cons: Two places to learn for one thing
More to build and keep in step
options.mitigation: Both draw from the same curve, so they never disagree.
